summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain centered at the G-tube site, symptoms that began after restarting tube feeds and changing the G-tube balloon. She was placed on bowel rest and received IV fluids. Over the course of five days, her symptoms improved, and she successfully advanced from clear liquids to a regular diet without complications. Her pain was managed with IV morphine initially, then transitioned to oral oxycodone. Psychiatry consulted for anxiety management but recommended against a clonidine patch due to low blood pressure. The patient was discharged home in stable condition, tolerating oral intake, with instructions to follow up with her bariatric surgeon before restarting tube feeds and to monitor for signs of dehydration or symptom recurrence.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection
